what_its_for: Eplerenone is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension) and to help protect your heart after a heart attack. It works by blocking a hormone called aldosterone, which helps lower blood pressure and reduce strain on your heart.
how_to_take: Take eplerenone by mouth with or without food. Swallow the tablet whole with a full glass of water. Try to take it at the same time each day to help you remember. Do not crush, cut, or chew the tablet unless your doctor tells you it is okay.
dosing: Your doctor will decide the right dose for you based on your condition. The usual starting dose is 25 mg once or twice a day. Your doctor may increase your dose to 50 mg once or twice a day after about 4 weeks. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and take your next dose at the regular time. Do not take two doses at the same time to make up for a missed one.
storage: Store eplerenone at room temperature, between 59°F and 86°F (15°C to 30°C). Keep it away from heat, moisture, and direct sunlight. Store it in the original container with the lid tightly closed. Keep all medicines out of reach of children and pets.
what_to_avoid: Avoid eating large amounts of foods high in potassium, such as bananas, oranges, potatoes, and salt substitutes that contain potassium, as this medicine can raise potassium levels in your blood. Avoid taking potassium supplements or other water pills (diuretics) unless your doctor approves. Avoid drinking grapefruit juice, as it can increase the amount of this medicine in your body and raise your risk of side effects. Avoid NSAIDs (like ibuprofen or naproxen) without checking with your doctor first.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor right away if you notice: muscle weakness, cramps, or pain; an irregular or slow heartbeat; feeling very tired or confused; numbness or tingling; chest pain; difficulty breathing; swelling of your hands, feet, or ankles; signs of high potassium such as nausea, weakness, or a feeling of heaviness in your legs. Also call if you feel dizzy or lightheaded, especially when standing up.
when_it_works: You may not feel any different when taking eplerenone because high blood pressure often has no symptoms. It may take several weeks to see the full benefit of this medicine. Keep taking it even if you feel well. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
special_populations: Older adults (65 years and older) may be more sensitive to this medicine and should be monitored closely by their doctor. Eplerenone is NOT recommended for use in children, as its safety and effectiveness have not been established in patients under 18 years old. Pregnant or breastfeeding women should talk to their doctor before taking this medicine, as its effects on an unborn baby or nursing infant are not fully known. People with kidney problems, liver problems, or diabetes should use this medicine with extra caution and will need regular blood tests to monitor potassium and kidney function.
